candidates.exact_span: Self-monitoring, sampling, reporting, notification and recordkeeping requirements, including an identification of the pollutants to be monitored (including the process for seeking a waiver for a pollutant neither present nor expected to be present in the Discharge on accordance with § 403.12(e)(2), or a 12specific waiver for a pollutant in the case of an individual control mechanism), sampling location, sampling frequency, and sample type, based on the applicable general Pretreatment Standards in 40 CFR 403, categorical Pretreatment Standards, local limits, and State and local law;
candidates.computation_change_reason: This clause defines operative monitoring elements (pollutants, locations, frequencies, sample types) and waiver pathways. Different readings of waiver eligibility, the ambiguous '12specific' wording, or the 'on accordance' phrasing change whether monitoring was required for a parameter (B) and whether missing results reflect documented non-requirement versus inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a pollutant is 'neither present nor expected' and whether the § 403.12(e)(2) waiver process applies determines if monitoring was required at all (B) and how to classify periods without reported results for that pollutant (C).

candidates.exact_span: Requirements to control slug discharges, if determined by the POTW to be necessary.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Slug-discharge controls are conditional on POTW determination. Different interpretations of whether such a determination was made change which enforceable limits apply (A) and whether related monitoring or plan obligations were triggered (B).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall evaluate, whether each Significant Industrial User needs a plan or other action to control slug discharges, in accordance with 40 CFR 403.8(f)(2)(vi);
candidates.computation_change_reason: This evaluation duty can spawn additional monitoring or reporting obligations for industrial users. Whether evaluation occurred and what it concluded affects which requirements were applicable (B) and how to interpret missing evidence when slug-control plans or associated monitoring were conditionally required (C).
